items.title: Was Elizabeth Holmes Guilty? What the Theranos Jury Actually Decided
items.description:
Theranos collapse explained from court and regulator records.
A jury convicted Elizabeth Holmes of defrauding investors, and acquitted her of defrauding patients. Using the Ninth Circuit's February 2025 opinion, the SEC's 2018 charges, the federal lab regulator's findings and reporting on the verdict and sentence, we show what the court record actually established: 12 tests on the Edison out of 300 developed, demos running a 'null protocol', drug-company logos added to reports, and a projected $230m profit against $1.94m of reported income.

Context: A24's documentary 'You Can See Everything' (Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim) about Holmes opens in US cinemas in October 2026. This episode is independent of the film and uses no footage, stills or quotes from it; it sticks to the court and regulator record.

Chapters
0:00 Cold open
0:58 One tiny drop
2:44 The demo room
4:10 What investors were told
7:19 The regulators arrive
9:40 What the jury decided
11:41 Prison and appeal
13:49 Our analysis
15:34 Outro

Sources
[1] US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, United States v. Holmes & Balwani, Nos. 22-10312, 22-10338, opinion filed 24 Feb 2025: https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2025/02/24/22-10312.pdf
[2] SEC press release 2018-41, 'Theranos, CEO Holmes, and Former President Balwani Charged With Massive Fraud' (14 Mar 2018): https://www.sec.gov/news/press-release/2018-41
[3] ABA Journal, 'Jury finds blood-testing company Theranos CEO Holmes guilty of fraud' (Jan 2022): https://abajournal.com/news/article/jury-finds-blood-testing-company-theranos-ceo-holmes-guilty-of-fraud
[4] CNBC via NBC, 'Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes sentenced to more than 11 years in prison' (18 Nov 2022): https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/business/money-report/former-theranos-ceo-elizabeth-holmes-sentenced-to-more-than-11-years-in-prison/3129509/
[5] MedCity News, CMS sanctions on Theranos (8 Jul 2016): https://medcitynews.com/2016/07/cms-fines-theranos/
[6] Bloomberg Law, 'Elizabeth Holmes gets a year knocked off her prison sentence' (26 Mar 2026): https://news.bgov.com/health-law-and-business/elizabeth-holmes-gets-a-year-knocked-off-her-prison-sentence

items.title: Why Did Northern Rock Collapse? £4.45bn Withdrawn in 3 Days
items.description:
Northern Rock collapse explained from court and regulator records: the 2007 bank run that opened Britain's 2008 financial crisis.
Savers withdrew £4.45bn in three days. Using the Treasury Committee's 'The run on the Rock', the Bank of England's statements, the FSA's own internal audit and enforcement notices, the National Audit Office's reports and the shareholder rulings up to Strasbourg, we show why a bank that was solvent on paper ran out of cash, which executives the regulator found failed to correct, or repeated, understated bad-loan figures, why shareholders were paid nothing, and what the rescue finally cost.

Chapters
0:00 Cold open
1:00 The bank that borrowed the world
2:43 The summer the market shut
4:20 The queues
5:57 The taxpayer steps in
7:45 Who was watching?
10:41 Worth nothing
12:29 Our analysis
14:49 Outro

Sources

items.title: First Brands: $5 Billion in Sales, $12 Million in Cash
items.description:
First Brands collapse explained from court and bankruptcy records.

The owner of Fram, Autolite and Raybestos sold about $5 billion of car parts a year. In September 2025 it filed for bankruptcy with $12 million in cash and more than $9 billion in liabilities. Using the US Attorney's charges, bankruptcy filings and lenders' own statements, we explain how invoice finance works, what prosecutors allege happened, what is still disputed, and who paid. Patrick and Edward James deny the charges and are presumed innocent; their trial is scheduled for February 2027.
